X3 and X4 are 'free lunch' inputs: increasing them improves Y1↑, Y2↓, and either Y3↑ (X3) or Y4↑ (X4).

X5 saturation was unexpected — the effect on Y1 is strongly nonlinear, with essentially zero additional gain above X5≈0.5. Below that, it provides ~0.3 units of Y1 improvement.
X1's effect on Y4, while small (0.058 range), showed clear saturation — gains almost stop above X1=0.55.

iteration_summaries.hypothesis: The system has 6 active inputs (X1-X6) and 6 inactive inputs (X7-X12). The system is STRONGLY NONLINEAR with multiplicative interactions. Y3 = f(X1, X3) with X1*X3 synergy — always satisfied at X1=1, X3=1 (Y3=0.997). Y4 = f(X2, X4, X6, X1_weak) with X2*X4 synergy and X6 negative. Y1 = f(all 6 active) with massive X2*X4 synergy, X2*X6 antagonism, and X5 sharp saturation at ~0.58 (gradient drops from 0.124 at X5=0.55 to 0.010 at X5=0.65 to 0.001 at X5=0.75). Y2 has CONTEXT-DEPENDENT effects: at high X2, X4 increases Y2 and X6 decreases Y2 (both reverse from low-X2 behavior). The Pareto frontier is a smooth 2D surface parameterized by (X2, X6) with X1=1, X3=1, X4=1, X5=0.55 fixed as universally optimal. X2 controls the Y1+Y4 vs Y2 trade-off (main axis). X6 controls the Y1 vs Y4 sub-trade-off at each X2 level (secondary axis). The model is now highly predictive — 10/10 predictions this iteration had errors <0.03 on all outputs.
new_findings: X5 saturates much more sharply than previously estimated: gradient drops from 0.124 at X5=0.55 to 0.010 at X5=0.65 to 0.001 at X5=0.75. Saturation occurs around X5≈0.58, not 0.75+ as previously thought. This means X5=0.55 is essentially optimal with negligible room for improvement.
All 10 gap-filling predictions were highly accurate: Y1 errors all <0.03, Y2 errors all <0.02, Y4 errors all <0.01. The causal model is very well calibrated.
